** πτό-ησις**,
or **πτοίησις** (so in {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus)}}, εως, ἡ, **vehement emotion** or **excitement**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Protagoras” 310d; περί τι [prev. author] “Smp.” 206d}}; ἡ τοῦ σώματος π. {{NT+4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Cra.” 404a, compare 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Generatione Animalium” 774a5 (uncertain), 4th-3rd c.BC: Clearchus Historicus (?) cited in 2nd c.AD: Athenaeus Epigrammaticus 15.670c, 2nd c.BC: Agatharchides Geographus 5, 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus 1.509; μὴ φοβούμεναι μηδεμίαν πτόησιν NT.1Pet.3.6.}}

4425:
** πτύον** [ῠ], τό,
**winnowing-shovel, fan**, {{Refs 8th c.BC+|8th c.BC: Ilias Homerus Epicus “Illiad” 13.588 (in poetry _genitive_ πτυόφιν), 4th-5th c.BC: Aeschylus Tragicus “Fragmenta - American Journal of Philology” 210, 5th c.BC: Sophocles Tragicus “Fragmenta” 1084, 3rd c.BC: Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus 7.156, 3rd c.AD: Porphyrius Tyrius Philosophus “de Antro Nympharum - Porphyrii Opuscula” 35}}:—**πτέον** is _Attic dialect_ _accusative_ to {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Aelianus Dion. “fragment” 288, 2nd c.AD(?): Pollianus Epigrammaticus 1.245, etc.}}
4426:
** πτύρομαι** [ῡ],
_aorist 2_ ἐπτύρην [ῠ] {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Fabius Maximus” 3}}, _infinitive_ πτυρῆναι {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Axiochus” 370a}}:—_passive_, **to be scared** or **frightened**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.25}}; of the soul, {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 8.45}}; especially of horses, **shy, start**, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 2.19}}, Plu.[same place]; τινι **at** a thing, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|[prev. author] “Marc.” 6; φωνῇ π. ὥσπερ θηρίον [prev. author] 2.800c; πρός τι 1st c.AD: Philo Judaeus Bybl. cited in 4th c.AD: Eusebius Caesariensis Scriptor Ecclesiasticus “Praeparatio Evangelica” 1.10: with _accusative_, π. τὸν θάνατον}} **start at, be alarmed at** death, Pl.[same place]; ἔν τινι {{NT|NT.Phil.1.28.}}
4438:
** πυκτ-εύω**,
_Boeotian dialect_ **πουκτ-**, **box, spar**, {{NT+6th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Xenophon Historicus “Respublica Lacedaemoniorum” 4.6, 4th c.BC: Demosthenes Orator 4.40; οὕτω πυκτεύω ὡς οὐκ ἀέρα δέρων NT.1Cor.9.26; π. καὶ παγκρατιάζειν 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Gorgias” 456d; περὶ τεοῦς Ἑρμᾶς ποτ᾽ Ἄρευα π. 6th c.BC: Corinna Lyrica 11}}; ἐς σὸν κρᾶτα π. **strike with the fist** on the head, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 229}}: generally, **fight**, ξιφήρη π. {{Refs 3rd c.AD+|3rd c.AD: Heliodorus Scriptor Eroticus 10.31}}; of gladiators, {{Refs|“Rev.Arch.” 30(1929).24 (from Gortyn)}}:—_middle_, πεπύκτευται αὐτόν {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd-3rd c.AD: Philostratus Sophista “Philostrati majoris imagines” 2.19.}}
4440:
** πυλ-ών**, ῶνος, ὁ,
**gateway**, {{Refs 4th c.BC+|4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “de Mundo” 398a16 (_plural_), “PCair.Zen.” 193.9 (3rd c.BC), “PEnteux.” 74.3 (3rd c.BC), “Sammelb.” 6157 (2nd c.BC), “IG” 3.398 (_plural_)}}; frequently separated from the house or temple to which it gave entrance, **gate-tower, gate-house**, {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|“IPE” 12.32 B 48 (Olbia, 3rd c.BC), 2nd c.BC: Polybius Historicus 4.18.2, 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Hipp.” 5, etc.}}; of a temple, {{Refs 1st c.AD+|1st-2nd c.AD: Plutarchus Biographus et Philosophus “Timoleon” 12}}; τετράθυρος π. {{Refs 3rd c.BC+|3rd c.BC(?): Callixinus Historicus 1; π. τὸ μῆκος δίπλεθρος 1st c.BC: Diodorus Siculus Historicus 1.47, compare 2nd c.AD: Lucianus Sophista “Nigr.” 23}}; ἡ θύρα τοῦ π. {{NT|NT.Act.12.13.}}
4445:
** πῠρέσσω**,
{{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Cyclops” 228}}; _Attic dialect_ **πυρέττω** {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 813, 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Theaetetus” 178c}}: _future_ πυρέξω {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “γυναικεῖα” 1.2}}: _aorist_ ἐπύρεξα {{Refs 4th c.BC+|[prev. author] “Prog.” 16, “Epid.” 3.17.ά, 4.26, +others, 4th c.BC: Aristoteles Philosophus “Physica” 228a28}}: _perfect_ πεπύρεχα {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|[prev. author] “Pr.” 901b10, 2nd c.AD: Marcus Antoninus Imperator 8.15}}:—_passive_, _perfect_ πεπύρεγμαι {{Refs 2nd c.AD+|2nd c.AD: Galenus Medicus 4.447}}: (πυρετός):—**to be feverish, fall ill of a fever**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Hippocrates Medicus “ἀφορισμοί” 2.28, 5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus [same place], 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Vespae” 813, 4th c.BC: Aeschines Orator 3.115, 2nd c.AD: Artemidorus Daldianus Onirocriticus 4.30, 4th c.AD: Sallustius Philosophus 9.}}
